stem.text: A function k satisfies \( \lim_{x \to \frac{13}{2}^{-}} k(x) = -\infty \). Describe in words what this statement says about k and about its graph.

answer_key.label: As x approaches \( \frac{13}{2} \) from the left, k(x) decreases without bound, so the line \( x = \frac{13}{2} \) is a vertical asymptote.

worked_solution.text: The input approaches \( \frac{13}{2} \) from the left only, and the output is not approaching any number.
worked_solution.rule_named: read the input side and the output behaviour

worked_solution.text: The values k(x) decreases without bound, which is what an infinite limit means, so the graph has the vertical asymptote \( x = \frac{13}{2} \).
